Academic Year 2023/24 Page 1 of 6 In-Class Test: Final Examination School Mathematics and Physics Module Title Tensor Analysis Module Code MTH3008 Module Coordinator Paula M Lins de Araujo Completion time 2 hours Scanning and uploading time 30 minutes Academic term End of 2nd term 2023/2024 General Instructions to Candidates 1. In sitting this examination you agree to comply with the University of Lincoln Code of Conduct in Examinations. 2. This assessment is a closed book exam, but you are allowed to bring one piece of A4 paper with hand-written notes on both sides. 3. You must submit only one version of your solution. You may cross out all workings that you do not want to be marked. 4. The examination must be completed within the completion time indicated above. Continuing past this time will be classified as misconduct in examinations. 5. The completion time may be different for students with Personal Academic Study Support (PASS). 6. Extensions do not apply, but Mitigating Circumstances can be applied for in the normal way. 7. After completion you must scan your work clearly (without blur) and in the correct upright portrait orientation for each page. 8. You must submit your answers as a PDF to Blackboard within 30 minutes of completion (Microsoft Lens can be used to scan the papers): 9. You must return the exam script and your written answers to an invigilator. 10. No collaboration or interaction with other individuals using any means of communication or device is permitted during the examination. 11. All work will be subject to plagiarism and academic integrity checks. In submitting your assessment you are claiming that it is your own original work; if standard checks suggest otherwise, Academic Misconduct Regulations will be applied.

Academic Year 2023/24 Page 2 of 6 Module-specific instructions 1. You must show all your workings. 2. Answer all questions. 3. The use of any electronic devices (including calculators) is not allowed.

# Page 3^page=3
Question 1 (a) Compute the outer product M ⊗ N of the following two matrices: [9 marks] M = ( 0 1 7 2 ) and N =   1 0 1 −1 −1 2   . (b) Suppose Tijkℓ is a rank-four tensor. [8 marks] (i) Write down the transformation rule of Tijkℓ. (ii) Using the transformation rule, show that Tijij is a scalar. (c) Let u, v, w, and z be vectors in R 3. Using suffix notation, find an expression [8 marks] involving no cross products for (u × (v × w)) · z. Write your final answer in vector notation. Provide all steps of your workings. Academic year 2023/24 Page 3 of 6

# Page 4^page=4
Question 2 In this question, denote by K the Cartesian coordinate system with vector basis i1, i2, i3, the standard orthonormal basis of R3. Denote by K ′ the coordinate system with vector basis e1, e2, e3 given by e1 = 2i1 + i3 e2 = i2 e3 = i1 − i2 + i3. (a) Find the dual basis e1, e2, e3. [8 marks] (b) Find the covariant and contravariant components of the vector V = 3i1−2i2+i3 [8 marks] with respect to the bases e1, e2, e3 and e 1, e2, e3. (c) Consider the second-order tensor of K with components [9 marks] [Pik] = [P ik] = [P ·k i ] = [P i ·k] =   0 2 0 3 0 −1 −1 0 1   . Express the covariant components of the given tensor in the coordinate system K ′. Academic year 2023/24 Page 4 of 6

# Page 5^page=5
Question 3 Consider the three-dimensional orthogonal coordinate system (x1, x 2, x 3) = (σ, τ, ϕ) with position r given by r = στ i1 + 1 2(σ2 − τ 2)i2 + ϕi3, where i1, i2, i3 are the usual Cartesian basis vectors. (a) Compute the basis vectors e1, e2, e3 of this coordinate system. [9 marks] (b) Compute the metric coefficients of the arc length and the components of the [8 marks] covariant metric tensor gii for the parabolic coordinate system. (c) Determine the following Christoffel symbols of the first kind for the parabolic [8 marks] coordinate system: Γ112, Γ123, Γ122, Γ233. Academic year 2023/24 Page 5 of 6

# Page 6^page=6
Question 4 (a) The third-rank tensor Tijk is symmetric with respect to its last two suffixes but [8 marks] antisymmetric with respect to its first and second suffices. Show that all entries of this tensor are zero (i.e. Tijk = 0, for all choices of i,j,k). (b) Let Vi be a (non-constant) covariant tensor. That is, it transforms according to [8 marks] the rule V ′ i = L k i′Vk. Prove that ∂Vi ∂xj is not a tensor, i.e. that it does not satisfy the transformation law of a tensor. You may use the formulas L k i′ = ∂xk ∂x′i , L i′ k = ∂x′i ∂xk . (c) Let f be a scalar field. Using suffix notation, evaluate the following expression [9 marks] ∇ × (∇f ).
